summary: Configured a persistent XFS filesystem at /srv/data with a filesystem-enforced 100 MiB quota for datauser. Verified enforcement before and after reboot without changing the installed RHEL release or kernel.
actions_performed: Mounted a dedicated XFS filesystem with user-quota enforcement and added it to /etc/fstab.
Set datauser's soft and hard storage limits to 100 MiB.
Confirmed a 110 MiB write fails with Disk quota exceeded.
Restarted node1 once and verified changed boot identity, recovered data, mount, and quota enforcement.
Removed test files; retained only the persistence marker.

evidence.summary: XFS user-quota accounting and enforcement are ON; datauser has 100M soft/hard limits, and an oversized write stopped at the limit.

evidence.requirement: Configuration persists while retaining the installed OS and kernel
evidence.summary: The mount, quota, owned data, RHEL 9.8 release, and 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 kernel remained intact after restart.

Captured healthy baseline with boot ID 377b5195-7fea-4219-a67b-044ef3f7ab99, acknowledged the native reboot, observed new boot ID 9167ea0b-ae69-431f-81c2-a7548eed3dd6, then proved mount, quota, data, and enforcement recovery.
